# Mark user-facing text with Fluentic

Use this file when converting an existing UI or reviewing whether text is translatable.

## Decision table

| Use case | API |
| --- | --- |
| Visible React text or rich content | `t.jsx(message, params?)` |
| String prop or non-React string API | `t.text(message, params?)` |
| Reusable message definition | `t.msg(message, schema?)` |
| One element with reactive translated string props | `t.jsx(() => element)` |
| Many reactive `t.text()` values in one component | `I18nState.use()` |
| Same source words with different meaning | `t.context(name)` |
| Translator instruction | `t.note(text)` |
| Structured JSON metadata | `t.meta(value)` |

Import without aliasing:

```ts
import { t } from '@fluentic/i18n';
```

## What to translate

Translate text a product user reads or hears: headings, body copy, navigation, buttons, links, form labels, placeholders, help text, validation errors, dialogs, toasts, loading states, empty states, error states, `title`, `alt`, and accessibility labels.

Do not translate user-generated content, server-returned content already localized by its owner, identifiers, routes, URLs, file paths, CSS classes, enum wire values, analytics event names, code, or developer-only logs.

## React content

```tsx
<h1>{t.jsx('Account settings')}</h1>
<button>{t.jsx('Save changes')}</button>
```

`t.jsx(message)` owns its language subscription.

## String props: whole component

```tsx
import { I18nState } from '@fluentic/i18n-web';

function SearchPanel() {
  I18nState.use();
  return (
    <section>
      <input
        placeholder={t.text('Search projects')}
        aria-label={t.text('Search projects')}
      />
      <button title={t.text('Clear search')}>{t.text('Clear')}</button>
    </section>
  );
}
```

Use this when several values depend on language or the component also needs i18n state.

## String props: one-element escape hatch

```tsx
function SearchField() {
  return t.jsx(() => (
    <input
      placeholder={t.text('Search projects')}
      aria-label={t.text('Search projects')}
    />
  ));
}
```

Only the wrapper reruns on language changes. The callback must return one React element. Keep hooks in the parent and capture their values; never call hooks inside the callback.

## Params, plurals, and reusable messages

Use ICU params, never concatenation:

```tsx
t.jsx('Welcome back, {name}!', { name });

t.jsx(
  '{count, plural, =0 {No messages} one {# message} other {# messages}}',
  { count },
);
```

Declare reusable param types once:

```ts
const welcome = t.msg('Welcome back, {name}!', { name: String });
t.text(welcome, { name: 'Ada' });
t.jsx(welcome, { name: 'Ada' });
```

Schema markers are `String`, `Number`, `Boolean`, and `Date`. Render calls receive real values, not constructors.

`t.params(object)` returns the same param object, or `{}` for nullish input. It is an optional typing/composition helper, not a translation marker.

## Context, notes, and metadata

Source text is the default identity. Add context only when identical wording has a different meaning:

```tsx
t.context('navigation').jsx('Home');
t.context('property-type').jsx('Home');
```

Chain translator guidance and JSON metadata:

```tsx
t.context('checkout')
  .note('Primary action after reviewing the order')
  .meta({ screen: 'checkout', priority: 'high' })
  .jsx('Continue');
```

Context contributes to identity. Notes accumulate. The last metadata value replaces earlier metadata.

## Rich content

```tsx
t.jsx('Read the <link>documentation</link>.', {
  link: t.tag((children) => <a href='/docs'>{children}</a>),
});
```

Keep the entire sentence in one message so translators can reorder tagged content.

## Static extraction rules

Good:

```ts
t.text('Saved successfully');
const saved = t.msg('Saved successfully');
```

Bad:

```ts
t.text(serverValue);
t.text(`Hello ${name}`);
const translate = t;
translate.text('Hidden from extraction');
```

For dynamic choices, define static descriptors:

```ts
const statuses = {
  active: t.msg('Active'),
  paused: t.msg('Paused'),
} as const;

t.jsx(statuses[status]);
```
